theme: ज्ञान-तृप्ति और समता: योग का आंतरिक मूल्यांकन। / Satisfaction through knowledge and equality: the inner standard of yoga.
context: The previous verse showed inner steadiness amid opposites. This verse gives a second sign of a mature yogi: the mind is nourished by wisdom and is no longer ruled by craving, comparison, or external status.
contextHindi: पिछले श्लोक में योगी की स्थिरता का वर्णन हुआ। इस श्लोक में योगी की दूसरी पहचान बताई गई है: वह ज्ञान से तृप्त है, और बाहरी मान-सम्मान, संपत्ति, या तुलना से उसके मन का शासन नहीं होता।
sanskritDevanagari:
ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः |
युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ||६-८||
transliteration:
jñānavijñānatṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ .
yukta ityucyate yogī samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ ||6-8||

wordByWord.meaning: One whose self is satisfied by knowledge and wisdom, not by external objects.
Unchanging, fixed, not moved by passing conditions.
One whose senses are controlled; not driven by compulsive impulse.
United, harmonized, established in disciplined awareness.
Seeing earth, stone, and gold alike; free from the ego’s comparative attachment to value.

spokenHindi: इस श्लोक में योगी की पहचान को ज्ञान और तृप्ति के शब्दों में कहा गया है। ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा का अर्थ है कि आत्मा अपने को सत्य, विवेक और अनुभव के भीतर समझकर तृप्त हो गया है। कूटस्थ यानी स्थिर, अचल, वह जो समय, भाव, और बाहरी बदलाव से नहीं हिलता। विजितेन्द्रियः का अर्थ है इन्द्रियों पर नियंत्रण। तब योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः होता है—वह मिट्टी, पत्थर और सोने को समान समझता है। यह बाहरी मूल्यांकन की समानता नहीं है, बल्कि भीतर की दृष्टि की समानता है: किसे धक्का लगाना है, किसका तिरस्कार करना है, किसमें अर्पण करना है, इन सब का निर्णय वह अहंकार से नहीं, विवेक से करता है। यह श्लोक हमें बताता है कि योग का लक्ष्य केवल एकांत में बैठकर ध्यान नहीं, बल्कि जीवन में अनुभूति है—जगह, वस्तु, प्रतिष्ठा, और धन को आत्मा के संदर्भ में देखने की क्षमता। जब हमारी तृप्ति बाहर से नहीं, भीतर से आती है, तब हम अपने स्वभाव से अधिक शांत, न्यायपूर्ण और समानदर्शी बनते हैं।
clearEnglish: This verse defines the yogi through inner satisfaction and equanimity. Jñānavijñānatṛptātmā means a self that is nourished by knowledge and wisdom, not by compulsive craving for gain, attention, or recognition. Kūṭastha points to the unchanging core of being, while vijitendriyaḥ indicates mastery over the senses and mental impulses. The line samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ is often misunderstood as moral indifference to all material values. It is better understood as a non-possessive equality: the one who sees that gold, stone, and earth are not sources of ultimate self-worth. This does not deny economic reality; it denies the ego’s habit of turning objects into identity. In modern life, this helps guard against status-hunger, comparison, and the idea that worth must be proven by possessions or prestige. A yogic mind becomes less reactive, less acquisitive, and more truthful. Its balance is not poverty of life; it is freedom from being ruled by what is seen, touched, or measured.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Text
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse explicitly describes a yogi as one who is satisfied by knowledge and wisdom, whose senses are controlled, and who sees gold, stone, and earth with equal inner regard. It is a portrait of inner freedom, not a rejection of ordinary life.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Inference
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: When value is measured by the Self rather than by possession, status, or comparison, choices become less compulsive and more ethical. This is not a denial of material life; it is a re-centering away from object-based identity.

practicalApplication.label: Value check
practicalApplication.text: Before buying, comparing, or seeking approval, ask: is this action driven by satisfaction, or by insecurity and image-making? This keeps attention on inner clarity rather than external comparison.

practicalApplication.label: Equal gaze
practicalApplication.text: Notice moments when you judge people or situations by status, beauty, money, or authority. Practice seeing them with a slightly wider perspective: each person is more than a social label.

reflectionQuestion: What in my life still makes me believe that worth must be proven through comparison, status, or possession?
reflectionQuestionHindi: मेरे जीवन में क्या ऐसी चीज़ है जो मुझे बताती है कि मेरी कीमत तुलना, पद, या संपत्ति से साबित होती है?
